topics.title: Failover
topics.summary: Choose backup accounts and models for supported provider failures.
topics.whenToUse: Optional: use backups when you want work to continue without waiting for you to select another account.
topics.behavior: Backups are tried in order, within the switch limit. Main-agent continuation and Reviewer/Advisor calls have different failure conditions; see each role for details.
topics.defaultBehavior: Off by default: zero switches or an empty backup list means no automatic alternative.
topics.impact: Backup accounts may have different costs and data handling. Changes apply to future launches, not running pods.
topics.example: Add a compatible second account and model, then allow one switch. The primary attempt does not count as that switch.

topics.title: Main agent failover
topics.summary: Continues work after a confirmed account usage or quota limit.
topics.whenToUse: Use a backup if the main account may reach its usage limit during a task.
topics.behavior: AutoPod settles the current execution and checks that work can be continued safely before trying a compatible backup. It does not switch automatically for general outages, authentication errors, failing tests or infrastructure problems.
topics.defaultBehavior: Without an enabled, usable backup, AutoPod pauses at a confirmed provider limit for operator intervention.
topics.impact: Continuation uses preserved work and a handoff; it is not an identical native conversation moved between runtimes. Task budgets are not reset.
topics.example: Your primary account reaches its confirmed usage limit. AutoPod can continue preserved work on the next eligible configured account.

topics.title: Reviewer failover
topics.summary: Retries supported authentication or provider-availability failures.
topics.whenToUse: Use backups to avoid losing an automated review to a supported provider failure.
topics.behavior: Isolated review calls try alternatives only for supported authentication or provider-unavailable errors when usage is measured. Retries share the call deadline. Unknown usage or unsafe execution is not permission for a blind retry.
topics.defaultBehavior: Follow main reuses the main route and its backups, but review-call failure rules still apply. Independent mode uses the Reviewer's own route.
topics.impact: Reviewer and Advisor calls share the reviewer token limit and whole-task accounting. A review finding does not itself trigger model failover.
topics.example: A review call reports a supported provider-unavailable error with measured usage. The next configured target can be tried within the remaining deadline.

topics.title: Advisor failover
topics.summary: Uses review-call retry rules for AI consultations.
topics.whenToUse: Use backups for supported provider failures during an AI consultation.
topics.behavior: Isolated Advisor calls use the same supported authentication/provider-unavailable retry conditions, measured-usage requirement and shared deadline as Reviewer calls. Selecting a route does not enable consultations; Workflow controls that.
topics.defaultBehavior: When Advisor is absent it follows Reviewer. Follow main or follow reviewer reuses that role's route; independent mode has its own backups.
topics.impact: Advisor and Reviewer share the reviewer token limit and whole-task accounting.
topics.example: An independent Advisor can have a backup account without changing the main agent's or Reviewer's configured route.

topics.title: Maximum failover switches
topics.summary: Limits how many automatic alternatives may be tried.
topics.whenToUse: Use a small limit to bound switching between backup accounts and models.
topics.behavior: The primary attempt is not a switch. A limit does not create extra backups; only configured alternatives can be used.
topics.defaultBehavior: 0 disables failover even when backup rows are saved. Supported range: 0–16.
topics.impact: A positive limit with no backups is still off. An enabled policy does not guarantee that a backup is eligible when needed.
topics.example: With two backups and a limit of 1, at most one automatic alternative is tried. Zero leaves both rows saved but inactive.

topics.title: Backup provider account
topics.summary: Chooses the enrolled account that authenticates and pays for this backup.
topics.whenToUse: Select an account with valid credentials for the intended provider and runtime.
topics.behavior: Each backup is a complete account, runtime, model and reasoning-effort selection. The account must remain available and compatible at execution time.
topics.defaultBehavior: No account is inferred from the model name. A saved unavailable account is retained for you to replace, not silently substituted.
topics.impact: Switching accounts can change billing and the provider handling task data. Selecting an account here does not sign in or create credentials.
topics.example: Select a second enrolled account, then choose a runtime and model supported by that account.

topics.title: Backup runtime
topics.summary: Chooses the agent integration used to run this backup.
topics.whenToUse: Match Claude, Codex, Copilot or Pi to the selected account's supported integration.
topics.behavior: Runtime is not the model or the account. AutoPod validates compatibility with the selected provider account.
topics.defaultBehavior: A displayed runtime is a selection, not proof that the account supports it.
topics.impact: Different runtimes can have different tools and session behavior; native conversation state is not copied unchanged between them.
topics.example: An Anthropic account normally uses Claude; an OpenAI account normally uses Codex.

topics.title: Backup model
topics.summary: Chooses the model requested when this backup is used.
topics.whenToUse: Choose an available model supported by the backup account and runtime.
topics.behavior: Enter the provider/runtime's model identifier. A model name alone does not supply credentials or select a provider account.
topics.defaultBehavior: The saved model is requested explicitly; the backup is not chosen simply because a different model might produce a better result.
topics.impact: Capability, token cost and data handling can differ from the primary model.
topics.example: Use an exact model identifier supported by the selected account rather than a display name copied from another provider.

topics.title: Backup reasoning effort
topics.summary: Adjusts reasoning effort where the selected runtime and model support it.
topics.whenToUse: Use higher effort for difficult work when additional latency and token use are acceptable.
topics.behavior: Auto leaves effort to the runtime default. Explicit low, medium, high or extra-high effort is subject to runtime/model support.
topics.defaultBehavior: Auto is the default; it does not mean that reasoning is disabled.
topics.impact: Higher effort can increase response time and token use. This is unrelated to the desktop's show-reasoning display preference.
topics.example: Keep Auto for normal work; choose High deliberately for a difficult backup task.
